acceptance_criteria: `Quantity { value: f64, dim: Dim }` where `Dim` holds integer exponents of length and angle (`Dim::NONE`, `Dim::LENGTH`, `Dim::ANGLE`; area is length²). Values are stored in base units: millimeters and radians.

`parse(src: &str) -> Result<Expr, ExprError>` accepts: decimal numbers (`5`, `2.5`, `.5`, `1e-3`), identifiers matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, binary `+ - * /`, unary minus, parentheses, and a unit suffix directly after a number or a parenthesized group (`5 mm`, `5mm`, `(d1 + 2) mm`). Units: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft` (length) and `deg`, `rad` (angle). Usual precedence and left associativity: `2 + 3 * 4 = 14`, `8 / 4 / 2 = 1`, `-2 * 3 = -6`.

`eval(&Expr, resolve: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Quantity>, default_length: Unit) -> Result<Quantity, ExprError>`. A bare number is unitless; the caller decides how to treat a unitless result (for example `5` typed into a length parameter). Test values: `1 in` = 25.4 mm exactly; `2 ft + 1 in` = 635 mm ± 1e-9; `90 deg` = π/2 ± 1e-12 rad; with `d1 = 40 mm`, `d1 / 2 + 5 mm` = 25 mm ± 1e-12; `d1 * d1` has dimension length² and value 1600.
`default_length` is how a result is *shown*: `Quantity::in_unit(Unit::In)` converts back, e.g. 25.4 mm → 1.0 in.

Errors, each with the byte offset in `src` where it applies, and a clear `Display`: syntax error (`2 +`, `(1`, `1 2`, `5 mmm`), unknown unit, unknown name (the resolver returned `None`), dimension mismatch (`5 mm + 2 deg`, `d1 + 3` where `d1` is a length and `3` is unitless), and division by zero. No panics on any input; a test feeds at least 20 malformed strings.
`Expr::names()` returns the identifiers an expression references, in first-use order without duplicates (`d1 / 2 + d1 * w` → `["d1", "w"]`), ready for the dependency ordering in M2-08b.
No `unsafe`; no new dependencies; `swx-core` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M2-08a: Parameter expressions with units: parse and evaluate `d1 / 2 + 5 mm` with unit checking
